title: Even as War Rages, Investors Bet Oil Will Be Cheaper in a Few Months
partialText: Futures contracts reflect an expectation that low inventories and midterm elections are likely to push the Trump administration to try to ease tensions with Iran.

title: Diesel Crisis Puts Poor Farmers Around the World at Risk
partialText: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has limited the shipment of diesel, depriving farmers of fuel for irrigation pumps and threatening the food supply.

title: Oil-Rich Saudi Arabia Isn’t Short on Energy. Here’s Why It Wants to Go Nuclear.
partialText: Opponents warn that a U.S.-Saudi deal could be a step toward the kingdom building an atomic bomb. But there are other reasons for the world’s largest oil exporter to diversify its energy mix.

title: Israel Welcomes Trump’s Demand for Diplomatic Ties With Saudi Arabia
partialText: Israeli officials greeted the possibility of normalized ties, but analysts said the U.S.-Saudi nuclear deal nonetheless remained bad for Israel. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has not yet commented on the agreement.

title: Trump Prepares Yet Another Strategy to Resurrect Global Tariffs
partialText: The administration’s 10 percent global tariffs are set to expire at midnight, but officials have been preparing replacements.

title: A Peptide Showdown: F.D.A. Scientists May Clash With R.F.K.’s Agenda
partialText: Agency scientists are advising against allowing widespread use of several peptide injections. Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the health secretary, has said people should be free to experiment.

title: Why I Sought Out a Taliban Commander I Had Fought
partialText: First as a Marine and then as a journalist, I spent years tied to Afghanistan. I returned one last time to speak to a former enemy in search of answers, and perhaps closure.

title: The Devotion of Willow Smith
partialText: The daughter of a Hollywood power couple, she has gone above and beyond to prove herself. Virtuosity and spiritual aspirations fill her latest, “The Thread.”

title: China Rewrites the ‘Soft Power’ Playbook for the A.I. Age
partialText: China is seeking global influence and good will with its open, low-cost artificial intelligence software.

title: Google Hit With $1 Billion Fine By EU Over Search Engine Practices
partialText: At a tense moment for trans-Atlantic trade, the European Union accused Google of anti-competitive business practices.

title: A New Target for Ukraine’s Long-Range Attacks: Russia’s Version of Amazon
partialText: Kyiv is escalating its air war by striking commercial warehouses, trying to bring the conflict closer to home for ordinary Russians.

title: Zelensky’s Dizzying U-Turn Is the Latest Zigzag in a Presidency Full of Them
partialText: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine has pivoted from unpopular moves before, but a recent decision about military leadership and strategy could weaken his position.

title: ‘We Will All Die From Ebola Here’: Virus Stalks Crowded Camps in Congo
partialText: There are a million people displaced by violence in the epicenter. They live in dangerous conditions and are fighting the virus with very little clean water.

title: Saying ‘Google It’ Makes You Sound Old. ‘Search It Up’ Instead.
partialText: As online research evolves, so has the language we use to describe it.

title: How to Use ChatGPT and Gemini Prompts to Find Out What They Know About You
partialText: It can be unsettling what Gemini and ChatGPT have figured out about you and how easily your privacy can be punctured. Here’s how to find out.

title: F.D.A. Announces New Cyclosporiasis Outbreak With 72 Cases
partialText: Health officials did not identify the location of the outbreak, or what they believed was causing it.

title: Amid Cyclospora Outbreak Tied to Lettuce, America Skips Salads
partialText: Foot traffic to chains such as Chopt and Chipotle fell in recent weeks after a recall from Taylor Farms and changing messages from the F.D.A.

title: Four Young Mathematicians Receive Prestigious Fields Medals
partialText: The awards are bestowed only once every four years to mathematicians under the age of 40.

title: ‘Odyssey’ Popcorn Buckets Help Fuel a $100 Million Market
partialText: Once, a tub of popcorn was just a tub of popcorn. Now, ‘collectible concession vessels’ could make one chain more than $100 million.

title: Gen Z Fell Out of Love With Work. I Don’t Blame Them.
partialText: For Gen Z college graduates, the way millennials lived out their ambitions no longer makes sense.

title: Iran, China, Canada? A Defense of Trump’s Grand Strategy
partialText: A Pentagon official argues that “people can no longer take the United States for granted.”

title: Photographic Evidence
partialText: We look at how The Times uses photographs and video to better understand what’s happening in the war with Iran.

title: ‘The Odyssey’ Hired Their Viking Ship. They Say It Came Back Damaged.
partialText: A Swedish Viking center said its vessel was used in the filming of Christopher Nolan’s epic but needed repairs when it was returned. Now, the center is seeking compensation.
